{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABeAg9IQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhHhxw0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 267, "title": "Launch saved graphs from the toolbar icon in independent Live windows; remove Launch Settings and simplify Graph Library", "body": "## Goal (approved UX)

Eliminate the fixed `Launch Settings` assignment UI. Choose a graph **where it is launched**, rather than in a global setup panel. The browser **extension toolbar icon** should start distinct saved graphs in **independent windows**, with **one graph/session per window**. Use the freed Graph Library space for a clean, graph-focused layout.

This complements #266 (Web-page microphone icon selection) and supersedes the fixed *Live Window* graph assignment UX from #243/#253/#260. **Do not add an unrelated launcher screen, dashboard, history, accounts, or complex new UI.**

## Extension toolbar icon: interaction

- **Left-click**: open a new Live/run window for the persisted **default Live graph** associated with the currently invoked tab. The window displays that graph and offers its existing Start/Stop controls. **Opening does not automatically begin capture or request microphone access.**
- **Right-click**: in Chrome's **native extension action context menu** (`chrome.contextMenus`, `contexts: ['action']`), list available saved runnable top-level graphs. **Selecting a graph opens a separate window for that graph**; do not just update a global assignment or switch an unrelated running window.
- Allow the **default for left-click** to be changed from this same native context menu in a minimal, clear way (e.g. a small default-selection submenu/entry). Keep **Run selected graph** distinct from **change default**: merely choosing a graph to open by right-click should not silently alter the left-click default unless the UI explicitly says it does.
- Preserve the user's selected default by stable graph ID across restart; migrate `assignments.live`. If it disappears or is invalid, handle it explicitly (choose the sole viable graph automatically if exactly one, otherwise show a minimal actionable selection path); never silently run the wrong graph.
- List only actual runnable top-level graphs; reject invalid/no-executable-path selections. Avoid treating reusable *subgraph definitions* (#265) as independently runnable unless supported as valid top-level graphs.
- Keep Chrome's own right-click/extension-management items intact. Use only the native context menu, no custom floating extension popup for graph selection. Add only the needed `contextMenus` permission. Account for Chrome action-menu capacity via one compact top-level submenu if there are many graphs, and refresh menu items when the library changes, the extension is installed/updated, or MV3 service worker restarts.
- Right-click menu item selection must preserve the **invoking tab** (and relevant activeTab user-gesture authorization) for the newly created window, rather than accidentally targeting whatever tab becomes active after focus changes.

## Independent windows / execution

- **One window = one chosen graph and one independent session.** Users can open Graph A, Graph B, Graph C in different windows and run them simultaneously. No arbitrary cap, single global Live-window reuse, global busy gate, or retargeting of an active window.
- Change `extension/background.js` behavior that currently searches all recorder TAB contexts and focuses the first existing `recorder.html` window. Each intentional launch creates an independently identified window/session with the explicitly selected graph ID and target tab.
- `extension/recorder.js` must load the selected graph for **that window** rather than always resolving `readLiveGraph(localStorage)` from a shared global assignment. The window's graph must remain stable during a running session; saved edits/subgraph changes may apply on next Start only, consistently with the existing snapshot semantics.
- Keep each window's source/tab targeting, graph actions (e.g. summary buttons), displays, workers, media streams, errors, Stop/cancel and cleanup scoped to that window. Closing one window must not close, cancel, or overwrite another. Preserve independent Live/Web execution from #256/#258.
- Respect actual Chrome tab-capture, microphone/device, permission and RAM/GPU limits; surface real per-window errors rather than reintroducing an artificial single-session restriction.
- Avoid shared-state races when multiple windows watch library storage, record selected tab, prewarm models or clean up after window closure.
- Keep the existing Live UI and behavior wherever possible; this issue is about choosing the graph and allowing several independent windows, **not** a redesign of the session display or a rename exercise.

## Remove Launch Settings, simplify Graph Library

- **Remove the entire `Launch Settings` panel** (not just the Live graph selector), including the obsolete `Live Window` dropdown, `Web Page Microphone` graph dropdown, help text/statuses and two-column empty settings layout.
- Keep Graph Library focused on **creating, finding, previewing, editing and managing graphs**. Use a simple, spacious, responsive single graph-list/workspace layout; eliminate the now-unused fixed-assignment filter/status UI where it no longer has meaning. Do not reintroduce the sidebar removed by #260.
- **Web microphone opt-in must remain explicit, default OFF and revocable** even after removing the Launch Settings panel. Relocate only the existing **Web microphone ON/OFF switch** plus required permission/status/help to a minimal, clearly labeled place in the existing Graph Library (e.g. compact header control/disclosure). Do not hide permission-sensitive settings, broaden website permission grants, or add a whole new settings page.
- Web microphone graph selection itself belongs on the **in-page mic's right-click menu**, per #266. Maintain its saved default and compatible-graph filtering; no replacement Web graph dropdown in Library.
- Keep the existing **Models** link, graph import/export, recovery, search/filter (except obsolete assignment-specific filter), and subgraph listing/editing from #265. Do not create extra navigation, marketing cards, tabs, or speculative features.
- Ensure responsive layout, keyboard access to context-menu alternatives where Chrome offers it, focus preservation, permission dialog accessibility, and clear error/empty states. Graph Library should not itself launch or bind a graph just by selecting a library card.

## Tests / acceptance criteria

- [ ] Left-click toolbar action opens a window with the saved default graph; opening is not auto-Start. Default persists across browser restarts and is changeable through the toolbar's native context menu.
- [ ] Right-click toolbar action lists saved runnable graphs; choosing one launches **that** graph in a new, distinct window, without unexpectedly changing the default.
- [ ] Three separate windows can run three different graphs at once; one window's Stop/close/failure does not affect the other two or independent Web dictation. Repeat launch does not focus/retarget an unrelated existing window.
- [ ] Launch target tab and needed `activeTab` permissions are correctly associated with each toolbar invocation, including context-menu invocation and focus changes.
- [ ] Missing/invalid/default-deleted graphs, graph-library edits, and subgraph references are resolved safely; already-running sessions keep snapshots.
- [ ] Graph Library no longer has a Launch Settings panel, Live/Web graph assignment dropdowns, assignment-only filter, or sidebar; graph management uses a clean uncluttered responsive layout.
- [ ] Web microphone ON/OFF, explicit consent, revocation, error/status guidance and #266 graph-selection behavior still work after relocating the switch.
- [ ] Graph Library Models access, graph management, save/conflict/import/export/recovery, and #265 subgraph workflows remain intact.
- [ ] Automated Chrome/MV3 UI tests cover action/menu events, default persistence, selected graph+tab per window, multiple simultaneous windows, independent cleanup, and streamlined library. Document tests actually run and manual-browser limitations honestly.

## Later manual checks

The completion criteria above use the applicable automated tests and normal review. The following native Chrome checks can be performed later. Their results are optional for review, merge, Issue closure, and Task completion. This supersedes the earlier review request to wait for these results.

- Try the native toolbar context menu and keyboard navigation in Chrome. Verify that graph selection opens the correct independent window, keeps the invoking tab and its `activeTab` access across focus changes, preserves the default graph, and retains Chrome's management items.
- Try the native permission dialogs in a fresh Chrome profile. Verify that opening Live does not request microphone access, denial leaves recording disabled, explicit consent permits recording, and disabling Web microphone access or revoking permission releases capture without stopping independent Live sessions.

Record actual coverage and the limits of automated tests. Keep the feature behavior and relevant automated checks specified above. Report any later manual results when available.

## References / coordination

- #266: in-page microphone left-click/run and right-click/set-default. Implement both features without confusing page-widget right-click (custom menu) with extension-toolbar right-click (Chrome native action menu).
- #260: completed sidebar cleanup; **this Issue replaces the remaining paired Graphs/Launch Settings layout with graph-only workspace**.
- #265: reusable shared subgraphs; resolve current definition at launch with safe graph snapshots.
- #263: no visible Web recording window; do not regress.
- #256 / PR #258: multiple independent Live/Web session foundations; preserve.
- Chrome context menu docs: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/contextMenus
- Chrome `activeTab` context-menu invocation behavior: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/get-started/tutorial/scripts-activetab

**Scope control:** Implement only these agreed launch interactions and the necessary Graph Library simplification. No separate generic Trigger/Event/Run Configuration UI, no new Graph Input/Output abstraction, no changes to graph processor architecture.
